A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with AdaRoute renamed ParaX in v2. All 17 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision-task evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements and feature visualizations in Section 4 and Appendices A–C.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original benchmark evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements and visual analyses, with limited revisions to reported settings and results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 specifies a router hidden layer of 16 channels instead of 24, a limited revision to the described model component. Shared expert centers, softmax routing, dynamic low-rank projections and multi-scale spatial mixing are otherwise unchanged; AdaRoute becoming ParaX is a rename.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ADE20K, COCO2017, CIFAR-100, SVHN, Food-101, ImageNet-R, Potsdam and LoveDA. Semantic, instance and panoptic segmentation, detection, classification, and the appendix pose-estimation and remote-sensing evaluations have unchanged coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons in Tables 1–4, 7–10 and 15 retain the same comparator sets. CoLoRA's revised score does not change baseline membership, and the newly cited dynamic-convolution methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 changes the reported router width from 24 to 16 channels, and Table 14(c) changes the tested widths from 8/24/40 to 8/16/40. Other splits, training schedules, metrics, backbones and measurement procedures remain unchanged. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing router-width sensitivity analysis in Appendix B.4 and Table 14(c) replaces its middle setting of 24 channels with 16 while retaining the associated scores and parameter count. The other ablations, efficiency analysis, ERF/CKA visualizations and expert-allocation analysis are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, run-to-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain efficiency averaging over more than 100 iterations and expert-activation averaging over the same image sample sizes.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes CoLoRA's ConvNeXt-L recognition quality from 50.6 to 59.6, while its PQ of 49.3 and SQ of 80.5 remain unchanged. Other outcome values are retained. Table 14(c)'s 47.3 APb and 42.7 APm are now associated with 16 rather than 24 hidden channels, so they do not demonstrate a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The expert-matrix definitions in Section 3.2 and the cross-layer gradient derivation in Appendix C.2, including Equations 1–3, are retained. No formal assumptions, proofs or mathematical results are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that shared parameter experts and input-dependent routing improve feature representation, cross-layer interaction and parameter-efficient visual adaptation. The abstract's shorter task summary and method rename do not substantively change the contribution or performance claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of expert allocation, cross-layer interaction, domain shift and dense-prediction limitations are retained. Appendix D preserves the limitations concerning inference integration, training latency and unevaluated larger models. Removing a duplicated explanation in Appendix B.4 does not change its meaning.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised future code release at a shortened link with a stated public release at a direct ParaX GitHub address. The documented router width also changes from 24 to 16 channels. Other implementation and hardware information is retained; repository availability and contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds KernelWarehouse and Omni-dimensional Dynamic Convolution citations in Section 3.2, plus HD-CNN, ConvNeXt V2, TransXNet and Vision Transformers Need More Than Registers in Section 2. These modestly expand attribution and background without changing the central novelty positioning or Appendix C.3 comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 renames AdaRoute to ParaX throughout, shortens the abstract's closing task description, adds an Appendix heading and publication notice, and makes localized wording and bibliographic edits. It also removes duplicated prose in Appendix B.4. The overall narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 receive revised labels, styling and trainable/frozen markers. Table 14 changes from three horizontally arranged panels to a vertical stack, and Tables 14–15 move from page 12 to a single-column arrangement on page 11. Other local spacing and float-placement changes retain the same figure and table inventory.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility information by replacing the future code-release promise with a stated public release and direct repository reference. Added dynamic-convolution attribution, clearer diagram annotations and editorial cleanup provide further modest benefits. The evidence base is largely unchanged, and the unexplained 24-to-16 router-width revision leaves uncertainty about the settings behind retained scores, limiting the overall gain.
